abstraction-with-base-interfaces.label: Abstract Base Classes and Interfaces
abstraction-with-base-interfaces.summary: Use `ABC` and `@abstractmethod` to make a shared method requirement enforceable, then make a subclass concrete by implementing that method.

try_abstraction_with_base_interfaces_ske.prompt: `CatalogItem` is already abstract and its constructor already stores `title`. In `models/book.py`, keep `Book` inheriting from `CatalogItem` and implement the required `label(self)` method so it returns `Book: ` followed by that object's title. Do not add another constructor; `Book` should inherit the parent's constructor. Leave `models/catalog_item.py` and `main.py` unchanged.
try_abstraction_with_base_interfaces_ske.hint: Implement the required method directly on `Book`. Once `label()` exists, Python can instantiate the child.

help.concept: A subclass remains abstract until it implements every required abstract method. Shared constructor setup can still be inherited.
help.hint_2: Define only `label(self)` and use the inherited `self.title`.

sc-interface-purpose.title: What does the abstract contract enforce?
sc-interface-purpose.prompt: What does `ABC` together with `@abstractmethod` add to `CatalogItem`?
sc-interface-purpose.hint: Think about what Python prevents when required behavior is missing.

help.concept: An abstract base class can prevent incomplete classes from being instantiated.
help.hint_1: The contract is about required behavior.
help.hint_2: Concrete subclasses can still implement that behavior differently.

options.a: Python blocks instantiation while a required abstract method is unresolved.
options.b: Every subclass must return exactly the same label text.
options.c: The abstract parent can no longer store shared state.
options.d: Subclasses are no longer allowed to inherit methods.

sc-interface-helper-focus.title: What happens to an incomplete child?
sc-interface-helper-focus.prompt: `CatalogItem.label()` is abstract. `DraftItem(CatalogItem)` does not implement `label()`. What happens when code tries to create `DraftItem("Notes")`?
sc-interface-helper-focus.hint: The child still has an unresolved abstract method.

help.concept: A subclass remains abstract until it implements every required abstract method.
help.hint_1: Inheritance alone does not make the child concrete.
help.hint_2: Python blocks construction of an incomplete child.

options.a: Python creates the object and uses `pass` as its label.
options.b: Python raises `TypeError` because the child is still abstract.
options.c: Python automatically copies a `label()` implementation into the child.
options.d: Python removes `CatalogItem` from the inheritance chain.

sketch-0.title: ABC turns a shared method into an enforceable contract

sketch-1.title: A subclass becomes concrete when it fulfills the contract
sketch-1.bodyMarkdown:
A concrete subclass satisfies the abstract contract by implementing the required behavior.

```python
class CashPayment(PaymentMethod):
    def pay(self, amount):
        return f"Paid ${amount} in cash"
```

Now CashPayment can be instantiated because it supplies the required `pay()` method.

The abstract parent defines what callers may rely on; the concrete child decides how that behavior works.
